summary.text: A patient with a history of hypertension, but no history of coronary artery disease, hyperlipidemia or smoking, presented with stab wounds to the left chest and systolic blood pressure in the 80s. In the trauma bay a chest tube was placed and the patient was intubated and transfused under the massive transfusion protocol, with systolic pressure stabilizing in the 130s.

The patient underwent a left anterior thoracotomy, left lower lobe wedge resection, a negative pericardial window and a negative exploratory laparotomy, with laboratory work grossly within normal limits. Shortly after leaving the operating room the patient had an inferolateral STEMI with elevated troponin and an anteroapical wall motion abnormality, and an acute proximal LAD thrombus was found and treated by aspiration thrombectomy without a stent.

After thrombectomy, heparin, aspirin, a beta blocker, Aldactone and an ARB were started for the STEMI, and a Cardene drip for hypertension. On hospital day 3 the patient was in hemorrhagic shock with hemoglobin 6.2 g/dL; heparin was stopped, two units of pRBCs were given and hemoglobin rose to 7.8 g/dL. CT showed no obvious active bleeding.

The patient self extubated on HD 4 and was alert and conversant. Hemoglobin remained stable, prophylaxis against deep venous thrombosis began on HD 5, and a repeat TTE on HD 7 showed normalization of the wall motion abnormality, consistent with resolution of myocardial stunning. The left chest tube was removed on HD 8, and the patient was discharged home after 9 days with no reported cardiac sequelae.
